facts.statement: Uberabasuchus was described based on a skull with jaws and a partial postcranial skeleton (specimen CPPLIP 630) found in Campanian to Maastrichtian sediments of the Marilia Formation in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
facts.quote: Fue descrito con base en un cráneo con la mandíbula y un esqueleto parcial postcraneal (espécimen CPPLIP 630) descubiertos en sedimentos que datan de las épocas Campaniense - Maastrichtiense de la Formación Marilia, en el estado de Minas Gerais.

facts.statement: Uberabasuchus possessed a high skull similar to sebecosuchians but had teeth with a circular cross-section.
facts.quote: It appears to have a high skull like that of the sebecosuchians, but differs from them in having teeth with circular cross-section.

facts.statement: Evidence from its postcranial skeleton and the arid climate of the region indicates Uberabasuchus was likely a terrestrial predator.
facts.quote: The post-crania and the geology suggesting an arid climate indicate that Uberabasuchus was likely a terrestrial predator.

facts.statement: Uberabasuchus had a triangular skull with a moderately narrow snout, round and large eye sockets.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Uberabasuchus es triangular con un hocico moderadamente estrecho. Las cuencas de los ojos son redondas y bastante grandes.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Uberabasuchus contained at least twelve teeth showing a certain degree of heterodonty.
facts.quote: Uberabasuchus tenía al menos doce dientes en la mandíbula, que tiene un cierto grado de heterodoncia.

facts.statement: The third tooth was the largest in the lower jaw, followed by nine smaller teeth of approximately equal size.
facts.quote: El tercera diente es el más grande de la mandíbula, seguido de nueve que son más pequeños y aproximadamente del mismo tamaño.

facts.statement: Uberabasuchus is classified within the family Peirosauridae.
The type species name U. terrificus combines the city of Uberaba with the Greek word for crocodile and the Latin word for terrible.
facts.quote: El nombre de las especie tipo de Uberabasuchus, U. terrificus, proviene de la ciudad de Uberaba, acompañada por la palabra griega souchos ("cocodrilo") y el latín terrificus ("terrible").

facts.statement: Later analyses contradict the hypothesis that Uberabasuchus is closely related to Mahajangasuchus, indicating they belong to different groups: Sebecia and Mahajangasuchidae respectively.
facts.quote: Análisis posteriores contradicen esta hipótesis, lo que indica que Uberabasuchus y Mahajangasuchus no están estrechamente relacionados, ya que Uberabasuchus pertenece al grupo Sebecia y Mahajangasuchus a una familia independiente, Mahajangasuchidae.

facts.statement: Uberabasuchus lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Uberabasuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous in the Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil.
rejected.quote: Uberabasuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph from the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil.

rejected.quote: Thus, rather than slicing flesh and blood vessels, it is likely to have inflicted powerful crushing bites.
